title: Book 1 — Clio, Chapter 34
paragraphs: After Solon had departed, a great retribution from God came upon Croesus, probably because he had judged himself to be the happiest of all men. First there came and stood beside him in sleep a dream, which revealed to him the truth of the evils that were about to come to pass concerning his son. For Croesus had two sons, of whom one was afflicted, being deaf and dumb, while the other far surpassed his peers of the same age in every way; and the name of this second son was Atys. Concerning this Atys, then, the dream signified to Croesus that he would lose him by the blow of an iron spear-point. When Croesus rose from sleep and turned the matter over in his mind, he was struck with fear on account of the dream. First he took a wife for his son, and whereas Atys had been accustomed to lead the armies of the Lydians, Croesus now no longer sent him forth on any such business. The javelins, lances, and all such weapons that men use in fighting he had removed from the men’s apartments and piled up in the inner bedchambers, for fear that something hanging on the walls might fall down upon his son.
